neighbours.label: anatomy of the pharyngeal arches and their derivatives (gills, branchial, aortic arch, parathyroid)
fire: Water passes over the gills of the young shark.
Each branchial cleft forms early in the embryo.
Doctors found a narrowing of the aortic arch.
Surgeons spared the parathyroid during the operation.
In fish embryos the pharyngeal arches give rise to the jaw.
Salmon breathe through gills on both sides.
The branchial arteries supply the head of the larva.
A tumor pressed on the arch of the aorta.
quiet: Water passes over the fins of the young shark.
Each finger forms early in the embryo.
Doctors found a narrowing of the left kidney.
Surgeons spared the spleen during the operation.
In fish embryos the spine gives rise to the tail.
Salmon swim upstream on both sides.
The leg arteries supply the foot of the larva.
A tumor pressed on the lining of the stomach.

notes: I tried this as a shared pattern behind the list (AGENTS.md 'a verb, not a list of nouns'). If it holds, the new cases are the test: 'pharyngeal arches' and 'branchial cleft' were not in the top examples.
